inscriptions.inscription_note: KAI 216 is reported as a twenty-line building inscription. The twenty line slots are preserved here, but the original script and transliteration still require verification against the primary edition. English translations are intentionally blank.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐤀𐤍𐤊 . 𐤊𐤕𐤌𐤅 . 𐤏𐤁𐤃 [.] 𐤐𐤍𐤌𐤅. [𐤆𐤉] . 𐤒𐤍𐤕 . 𐤋[𐤉] . 𐤍𐤑𐤁 . 𐤁

inscription_lines.english_translation: I am KTMW (Kuttamuwa), servant of Panamuwa, who commissioned this stele for myself while I was still...

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐤇𐤉𐤉 . 𐤅𐤔𐤌𐤕 . 𐤅𐤕𐤄 . 𐤁𐤎𐤉𐤓\𐤃 . 𐤏𐤋𐤌𐤉 . 𐤅𐤇𐤂𐤂𐤕 . 𐤎

inscription_lines.english_translation: ...alive and placed it in an eternal chamber; I established a feast in that chamber:

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐤉𐤓\𐤃 . 𐤆𐤍 . 𐤔𐤅𐤓 . 𐤋𐤄𐤃𐤃 . 𐤒𐤓\𐤃𐤐𐤃\𐤓𐤋 . 𐤅𐤉𐤁𐤋 . 𐤋𐤍𐤂
inscription_lines.transliteration: yr/d . zn . šwr . lhdd . qr/dpd/rl . wybl . lng
inscription_lines.english_translation: a bull for Hadad Qarpatalli, a ram for NGD/R ṢWD/RN, and a ram...

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐤃\𐤓 . 𐤑𐤅𐤃\𐤓𐤍 . 𐤅𐤉𐤁𐤋 . 𐤋𐤔𐤌𐤔 . 𐤅𐤉𐤁𐤋 . 𐤋𐤄𐤃𐤃 . 𐤊𐤓𐤌𐤍
inscription_lines.transliteration: d/r . ṣwd/rn . wybl . lšmš . wybl . lhdd . krmn
inscription_lines.english_translation: ...for Šamš, a ram for Hadad of the Vineyards, and a ram...

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐤅𐤉𐤁𐤋 . 𐤋𐤊𐤁𐤁𐤅 . 𐤅𐤉𐤁𐤋 . 𐤋𐤍𐤁𐤔𐤉 . 𐤆𐤉 . 𐤁𐤍𐤑𐤁 . 𐤆𐤍 .
inscription_lines.transliteration: wybl . lkbbw . wybl . lnbšy . zy . bnṣb . zn .
inscription_lines.english_translation: ...for Kubaba, and a ram for my soul (NBŠ), which will be in this stele.
From now on, whichever of my sons—or...
...whichever son of another person—comes to possess this chamber, let him...
...take for the offering from the best produce of this vineyard...
...as a presentation offering, year after year.
He must also carry out the slaughter described above...
...near my soul...
...and apportion...
...a leg-cut for me.

inscriptions.inscription_note: The inscription is Aramaic written in the Phoenician alphabet. The 13 line divisions below follow the line breaks reproduced in the Wikipedia article’s transcription of Pardee (2009). The English is a cautious line-by-line segmentation and paraphrase of the article’s continuous translation, not a new critical edition; uncertain divine names and readings are retained.

inscription_lines.transliteration: znh ntn hdd mn ʿnq lmrʾn hzl bšnt ʿbr mrʾn nhr
inscription_lines.english_translation: [This is] what Hadad has given from Unqi to our lord Hazael in the year when our lord had crossed the river.

inscriptions.inscription_note: The artifact carries one continuous Phoenician inscription of 36 characters, read from right to left after rotation. The relief divides it visually into sequences of 25 and 11 characters, but the inscription has no word separators; the script and transliteration below are a normalized reconstruction from the published reading and should be treated cautiously.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡆𐡉 𐡉𐡄𐡍𐡎 𐡀𐡉𐡕 𐡍𐡑𐡁[𐡀] 𐡆𐡍𐡄 [𐡌𐡍 𐡀𐡔𐡓𐡄]

in war or in peace, any kind of pestilence, [as]

inscription_lines.transliteration: hʾ lḥldy zy bzʿtr šbʿ šwrh

inscription_lines.transliteration: yhynqn ʿgl ḥd wʾl yšbʿ wšb
inscription_lines.english_translation: nurse one calf and may it not be satiated. And may seven

inscription_lines.transliteration: ʿ nšn yʾpw btnr ḥd[ ] wʾl ymlʾ
inscription_lines.english_translation: women bake in one oven and may they not fill

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡅𐡄𐡉 𐡅𐡉𐡀𐡁𐡃 𐡌𐡍 𐡌𐡕𐡄 𐡕𐡍𐡍 𐡀𐡔𐡄 𐡅𐡒𐡋

inscription_lines.english_translation: it. And may vanish from his country the smoke of a furnace and the sound of
a mill. And may his land be salted and may sway back and forth

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡃𐡄 𐡐𐡓𐡏 𐡓𐡀𐡔 𐡅𐡌𐡋𐡊𐡀 𐡄𐡀 𐡆𐡉 [𐡉𐡊𐡕]𐡁

inscription_lines.english_translation: in it the crack of an earthquake. And that king who would [write]

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡏𐡋 𐡍𐡑𐡁𐡀 𐡆𐡍[𐡄] 𐡊𐡓𐡎𐡀𐡄 𐡉𐡄𐡐𐡊𐡄 𐡄𐡃[𐡃]

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡅𐡇𐡋𐡃𐡉 𐡅𐡔𐡁𐡏 𐡔𐡍𐡉𐡍 𐡀𐡋 𐡉𐡕𐡍 𐡄𐡃𐡃 𐡒[𐡋𐡄]

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡁𐡌𐡕𐡄 𐡅𐡉𐡌𐡇𐡀𐡄𐡉 𐡊𐡋 𐡋𐡅𐡑 𐡍𐡑[𐡁𐡀] 𐡆𐡍𐡄

inscriptions.inscription_note: The Qalaichi/Bukan find is reported as a unique 13-line Aramaic inscription. The accessible Qalaichi and Cambridge sources confirm the line count and context but do not publish a verifiable line-by-line original-script edition. The transcription, transliteration, and translation are therefore left pending against the primary publications and facsimile.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡔𐡋𐡌 𐡁𐡉𐡕 𐡍𐡁𐡅 𐡀𐡋 𐡀𐡇𐡉 𐡐𐡎𐡌𐡉 𐡁𐡓 𐡍𐡁𐡅𐡍𐡕𐡍 𐡌𐡍 𐡀𐡇𐡅𐡊 𐡌𐡊𐡉𐡁𐡍𐡉𐡕
inscription_lines.transliteration: šlm byt nbw ʾl ʾḥy psmy br nbwntn mn ʾḥwk mkbnyt
inscription_lines.english_translation: The peace of the temple of Nabu be upon my brother Psami, son of Nabunathan, from your brother Makkibanit.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡁𐡓𐡊𐡕𐡊 𐡋𐡐𐡕𐡇 𐡃𐡉 𐡉𐡇𐡆𐡍𐡉 𐡀𐡐𐡉𐡊 𐡁𐡔𐡋𐡌
inscription_lines.transliteration: brktk lptḥ dy yḥzny ʾpyk bšlm
inscription_lines.english_translation: I bless you by Ptah, that he may allow me to see your face in peace.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡅𐡊𐡏𐡍 𐡇𐡓𐡅𐡆 𐡔𐡋𐡌 𐡄𐡅 𐡕𐡍𐡄 𐡀𐡋 𐡕𐡃𐡇𐡋 𐡋𐡄
inscription_lines.transliteration: wkʿn ḥrwz šlm hw tnh ʾl tdḥl lh
inscription_lines.english_translation: And now: Haruz is doing well here; do not worry about him.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡊𐡋 𐡌𐡄 𐡃𐡉 𐡕𐡅𐡊𐡋𐡅𐡍 𐡋𐡏𐡁𐡃 𐡋𐡄 𐡀𐡍𐡄 𐡏𐡁𐡃
inscription_lines.transliteration: kl mh dy twklwn lʿbd lh ʾnh ʿbd
inscription_lines.english_translation: Whatever you are able to do for him, I am doing.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡅𐡊𐡏𐡍 𐡄𐡁𐡅 𐡋𐡉 𐡆𐡉𐡕𐡀 𐡅𐡌𐡔𐡇𐡀 𐡃𐡉 𐡔𐡋𐡇𐡕𐡅𐡍 𐡋𐡉
inscription_lines.transliteration: wkʿn hbw ly zytʾ wmšḥʾ dy šlḥtwn ly
inscription_lines.english_translation: And now: give me the olive oil and the oil that you sent for me.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡔𐡋𐡌 𐡌𐡌𐡄 𐡀𐡌𐡉 𐡅𐡔𐡋𐡌 𐡊𐡋 𐡁𐡉𐡕𐡀
inscription_lines.transliteration: šlm mmh ʾmy wšlm kl bytʾ
inscription_lines.english_translation: Greetings to Mama, my mother, and greetings to the whole household.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡔𐡋𐡌 𐡀𐡇𐡉 𐡅𐡁𐡍𐡉 𐡅𐡔𐡋𐡌 𐡊𐡋 𐡔𐡊𐡍𐡉𐡀
inscription_lines.transliteration: šlm ʾḥy wbny wšlm kl šknyʾ
inscription_lines.english_translation: Greetings to my brothers and my children, and greetings to all the neighbors.
I have sent this letter to inquire of your welfare.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡀𐡋 𐡀𐡁𐡉 𐡐𐡎𐡌𐡉 𐡁𐡓 𐡍𐡁𐡅𐡍𐡕𐡍 𐡌𐡍 𐡌𐡊𐡉𐡁𐡍𐡉𐡕
inscription_lines.transliteration: ʾl ʾby psmy br nbwntn mn mkbnyt
inscription_lines.english_translation: To my father Psami, son of Nabunathan, from Makkibanit.
To be delivered to Syene.

inscriptions.inscription_note: The 15 pending line slots follow the published recto/verso line count for TAD A2.4 (10 recto and 5 verso). Original script, transliteration, and English translation are intentionally left blank pending verification against the primary edition.

inscription_lines.english_translation: The vessel which Pīf-ittanni daughter of ʾElsatar made
for ʿAtarmasornu son of NGŠ.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡔𐡍𐡍 𐡉 𐡐𐡕𐡉𐡕𐡅 𐡏𐡁𐡉𐡃 𐡆𐡉 𐡌𐡓𐡀𐡍 𐡐𐡓𐡉𐡃𐡀𐡓𐡔 𐡌𐡋𐡊𐡀 𐡒𐡔𐡉𐡈𐡀
inscription_lines.transliteration: šnn y ptytw ‘byd zy mr’n pryd’rš mlk’ qšyṭ’
inscription_lines.english_translation: Ten years having passed (?). It so happened (?) that our lord, King Priyadarśin, became the institutor of Truth.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡌𐡄𐡒𐡔𐡈𐡌𐡍 𐡀𐡃𐡉𐡍 𐡆𐡏𐡉𐡓 𐡌𐡓𐡏𐡀 𐡋𐡊𐡋𐡄𐡌 𐡀𐡍𐡔𐡍 𐡅𐡊𐡋𐡄𐡌 𐡀𐡃𐡅𐡔𐡉𐡀 𐡄𐡅𐡁𐡃𐡅𐡁𐡊𐡋 𐡀𐡓𐡒𐡀 𐡓𐡀𐡌 𐡔𐡕𐡉
inscription_lines.transliteration: mhqšṭmn ’dyn z‘yr mr‘’ lklhm ’nšn wklhm ’dwšy’ hwbdwbkl ’rq’ r’m šty
inscription_lines.english_translation: Since then, evil diminished among all men and all misfortunes were caused to disappear; and there was peace as well as joy throughout the whole earth.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡅𐡀𐡐 𐡆𐡉 𐡆𐡍𐡄 𐡊𐡌𐡀𐡊𐡋𐡀 𐡋𐡌𐡓𐡀𐡍 𐡌𐡋𐡊𐡀 𐡆𐡏𐡉𐡓𐡒𐡈𐡋𐡍
inscription_lines.transliteration: w’p zy znh km’kl’ lmr’n mlk’ z‘yrqṭln
inscription_lines.english_translation: Moreover, there was this concerning food: for our lord the king, only a few animals were killed.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡆𐡍𐡄 𐡋𐡌𐡇𐡆𐡄 𐡊𐡋𐡄𐡌 𐡀𐡍𐡔𐡍 𐡀𐡕𐡄𐡇𐡎𐡉𐡍𐡍 𐡀𐡆𐡉 𐡍𐡅𐡍𐡉𐡀 𐡀𐡇𐡃𐡍𐡀𐡋𐡊
inscription_lines.english_translation: Having seen this, all men gave up the slaughter of animals; even those men who catch fish—the fishermen—were subject to prohibition.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡀𐡍𐡔𐡍 𐡐𐡕𐡉𐡆𐡁𐡕 𐡊𐡍𐡌 𐡆𐡉 𐡐𐡓𐡁𐡎𐡕 𐡄𐡅𐡉𐡍 𐡀𐡋𐡊
inscription_lines.english_translation: Similarly, those who were without restraint ceased to be without restraint.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡀𐡕𐡄𐡇𐡎𐡉𐡍𐡍 𐡌𐡍𐡐𐡓𐡁𐡎𐡕𐡉 𐡅𐡄𐡅𐡐𐡕𐡉𐡎𐡕𐡉 𐡋𐡀𐡌𐡅𐡄𐡉 𐡅𐡋𐡀𐡁𐡅𐡄𐡉 𐡅𐡋𐡌𐡆𐡉𐡔𐡕𐡉𐡀
inscription_lines.english_translation: And obedience to mother, father, and old men reigned in conformity with the obligations imposed by fate on each person.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡀𐡍𐡎𐡍𐡀𐡉𐡊 𐡀𐡎𐡓𐡄𐡉 𐡇𐡋𐡒𐡅𐡕𐡀 𐡅𐡋𐡀 𐡀𐡉𐡕𐡉 𐡃𐡉𐡍𐡀 𐡋𐡊𐡋𐡄𐡌 𐡀𐡍𐡔𐡉𐡀 𐡇𐡎𐡉𐡍𐡆𐡍𐡄 𐡄𐡅𐡕𐡉𐡓
inscription_lines.transliteration: ’nsn’yk ’srhy ḥlqwt’ wl’ ’yty dyn’ lklhm ’nšy’ ḥsynznh hwtyr
inscription_lines.english_translation: And there was no Judgment for all the pious men.
This, the practice of Law, has been profitable to all men and will be more profitable in future.

inscriptions.inscription_note: The inscription is highly fragmentary. The 12 line divisions below follow the published table; translations are possible interpretations, and ellipses mark missing or uncertain text.

inscription_lines.english_translation: [No?] living [being] is to be fattened [with other living beings?] …
… to be for people (that is, existing people) …
… to be seen—it is said—not [good] …
[… increase] of this object (that is, the practice of Dharma)—it is said—[caused] to increase …
… to see, to be seen—it is said …
… of the Beloved of the Gods [when] consecrated [for eight years]—it is said …
… in [outlying] towns—it is said … [all these instructions] were set (or put) to writing on pillars …

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡁𐡔𐡍𐡕 𐡛 𐡗 𐡇𐡆𐡉 𐡗 𐡐𐡓𐡉𐡃𐡓𐡔 𐡌𐡋𐡊𐡀 𐡗 𐡓𐡒 𐡃𐡇𐡀

inscription_lines.english_translation: In the year 10, behold, the king Priyadasi expelled vanity from among prosperous men,
friends of that which is vain,

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡌𐡍 𐡔𐡓𐡉𐡓𐡉𐡍 𐡃𐡅𐡃𐡉 𐡌𐡄 𐡏𐡁𐡃 𐡓𐡉𐡒 𐡒𐡔𐡕𐡍
inscription_lines.transliteration: mn šryryn dwdy mh ʿbd ryq qštn
inscription_lines.english_translation: friends of those who fish fish-creatures.

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡙 𐡝 𐡆𐡍𐡄 𐡕𐡌𐡄 𐡕𐡃𐡌𐡓 𐡔𐡌𐡄 𐡆𐡍𐡄 𐡀𐡓𐡄𐡀 𐡊𐡍𐡐𐡕𐡉 𐡎𐡄𐡕𐡉
inscription_lines.transliteration: 200 znh rmh Tdmr šmh znh ʾrʾ knpty shty
inscription_lines.english_translation: At 200 ‘bows’, there is over there the place called Tadmor. This is the KNPTY road, that is to say (the road) of the Garden:

inscription_lines.original_script: 𐡂𐡍𐡕𐡀 𐡉𐡕𐡓𐡉 𐡝 𐡜 𐡕𐡓𐡕𐡀 𐡕𐡍𐡄 𐡝 𐡏𐡋𐡀 𐡜 𐡜 𐡜 𐡜
inscription_lines.english_translation: More than 120 (‘bows’). At TRT’, here: 100. Above: 80.
Done with Wasu the judge
In commemoration of the One whose name is blessed.
Zabd'ateh, son of Hagagu, made it.
He was the son of Bar'ateh 'Alayb'al.

inscriptions.inscription_note: The inscription is Aramaic in the East Syriac (Estrangela) script. Line 1 is the Trinitarian invocation heading the stele above the Chinese text. Line 4 (Adam/Jingjing) is a quoted Unicode reading. For lines 2–3 and 5–7 the Syriac columns give editorial reconstructions of the personal names and titles, spelled from well-attested Classical Syriac forms, because the checked public witnesses (Hall 1895; Havret facsimile) preserve the stone's Syriac only as printed or facsimile images and their OCR is unreliable; these reconstructed cells should be verified against the facsimile and are not a diplomatic transcription of the exact letter forms and word order on the stone. Lines 8–14 give the side-edge name lists grouped by Hall's seven columns (Classis I–VII); the English and transliterated names follow Hall 1895, while the Syriac spellings are editorial reconstructions of those names. Name readings vary across editions (for example Yazedbuzid/Iezdebuzid/Yesbuzid and Sabar Jesus/Sabranieshuʿ). Sources: Isaac H. Hall, "The Syriac Text of the Chinese Nestorian Tablet," American Journal of Semitic Languages and Literatures 12 (1895), pp. 119–125; Henri Havret, La Stèle Chrétienne de Si-ngan-fou, facsimile edition.

this boundary here in front of

inscriptions.inscription_note: The eight-line division follows the published transcription reproduced by Persée. The original-script column preserves the supplied Hebrew-character transcription; it should not be treated as a diplomatic Unicode rendering of the carved stone. The transliteration retains the uncertain slash in PWŠD/R and the supplied place-name readings.
